title: Sterling Row luxury-listing channel: grade eight mixed-light property stills to one prestige house look on an in-frame grey card, author the per-episode thumbnail set by data-merge, and cut the flagship teaser + end card
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief: a top-producing luxury real-estate broker's online video channel (market-insight + property-walkthrough videos, 3-4/month) needs a per-video content package — a click-worthy on-brand thumbnail that is NOT a generic headshot-with-a-text-box, a cinematic cold-open teaser cross-postable as a 1:1 square, and a consistent branded end card — with luxury-brand restraint and a 48-72h turnaround. The real post named no company; the brokerage is laundered to a fictional wordmark, 'STERLING ROW', and the broker stays an unnamed figure (Manhattan/Tribeca are real places, and the 16:9 video-platform and 1:1 square are generic delivery-format descriptors, no named platform is the client). REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to fix the killed original (which punted the whole designed thumbnail — the headline TYPE — to 'one local packaging step' a human does, and which built the teaser/end-card by POOLING several short clips, an assembly the connector cannot do): the channel is modeled as needing a repeatable THUMBNAIL SYSTEM, not one hand-off. The broker supplies a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record thumbnail template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> for the episode headline/tagline/price teaser and THREE @-prefixed image-path columns (the per-episode graded property hero, the shared isolated broker figure, and the shared vectorized wordmark), plus an episode roster CSV, a studio portrait, a flat wordmark PNG, EIGHT existing property hero stills shot across different listings under deliberately mismatched light each carrying an 18% grey card in frame, one genuinely-long walkthrough camera take, and one long 4K skyline backplate take. The Adobe chain does the real paid work: neutralize every still to its own in-frame grey card so the whole channel shares one prestige white point, author a signature luxury look on the flagship still and match the rest to it, isolate the broker, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, data-merge the authored template so every episode's headline is ACTUALLY SET onto its finished thumbnail, and shorten the two long takes into the teaser and end card. Nothing is invented that the brief did not ask for; the eight-still count, the in-frame grey card, the per-listing lighting split, and the exact pixel targets are benchmark enrichment consistent with the source.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-light luxury-listing hero stills to the 18% grey card each one carries so the channel reads as one set, author a prestige house look on the flagship still and match the other seven to it, isolate the broker and vectorize the wordmark, data-merge the client's authored thumbnail template so each episode's headline is set onto its own finished thumbnail, and shorten the long walkthrough take and long skyline backplate into a cold-open teaser (16:9 video-platform + 1:1 square cross-post) and a branded end card.
full_brief:
STERLING ROW is a luxury-listing online video channel. We publish 3-4 videos a month and every one needs the same three things, built to one consistent prestige look, in 48-72h: a click-worthy thumbnail that is on-brand for high-end property (NOT a generic headshot with a text box slapped on), a cinematic cold-open teaser that hooks in the first five seconds and hard-cuts before the reveal (also cross-posted as a 1:1 square), and a branded end card with room for a subscribe prompt, a suggested-video card and a CTA that stays identical episode to episode.

We are NOT reshooting. Here is the problem and the whole job. We are handing you EIGHT existing property hero stills, one per upcoming episode's featured listing, and they do not match: they were taken in different rooms in different buildings under whatever light each space had — some cool, some warm, some flat, one shot late so the room is bright and blown, one shot dim. Straight out of the folder a row of thumbnails built from these looks like a cheap mismatched channel, and that kills click-through. To make consistency checkable we laid an 18% grey card into a corner of every still. Your job on the stills: bring the whole set to ONE prestige house look by neutralizing each frame to the grey card it carries — the card must read as clean neutral (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole channel shares one white point. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the eight: each room was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target, and you must hand back the final moves you dialed on each frame so we can confirm the set was matched rather than eyeballed. Be careful: at least one listing's warmth is the actual selling feature (a terrace caught at golden hour, an amber glow we are selling) — if its grey card already reads neutral, do not scrub that character chasing a cool cast you imagine. On the flagship listing (the Tribeca penthouse great room, our page-one thumbnail) go further and AUTHOR the signature Sterling Row look: a moody high-contrast luxury grade — deep blacks that never crush to pure zero, controlled window highlights, a restrained warm prestige feel, and the city skyline through the glass lifted so it glows without turning garish — and then match the other seven to that look, not just to neutral. This is the distinctive thing the channel is paying for; it must be a look you build, not a canned filter.

Thumbnail assembly: we have hand-built the InDesign thumbnail template with the real placeholder fields (episode headline, listing tagline, price teaser) and three image slots (the graded property hero, a small isolated figure of the broker, and the wordmark riding a light masthead band across the top). We are giving you the episode roster. Merge them so every episode gets its own finished 1280x720 thumbnail with its headline actually set, its graded hero dropped in, the broker figure and the crisp wordmark placed — hand back one thumbnail-set PDF, one finished thumbnail per episode, the flagship penthouse first. To feed that merge, isolate the broker cleanly from his studio backdrop as a transparent figure, and clean our wordmark (it only exists as a flat raster) into a razor-sharp vector so it prints crisp at any size on the sheet.

Video: from our single long walkthrough take of the flagship penthouse, give us the most compelling short cold-open cut (a strong hook in the first five seconds, hard-cut before the reveal) as the 16:9 video-platform-native teaser, then reframe that exact cut to a 1:1 square cross-post without changing its length. And from our long skyline backplate take, give us a short branded end-card cut reframed to our exact delivery frame with the lower third kept clear for the subscribe/suggested-video/CTA, consistent across every episode.

Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one prestige white point with the flagship look holding across all eight; the broker cleanly isolated; the wordmark a crisp vector; every roster episode a finished captioned thumbnail (one page each, flagship first); the teaser hooking early and hard-cutting; the end card at exact frame with its lower third clear.

inputs.name: hero_01_penthouse_greatroom.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a Tribeca penthouse great room at blue hour, ~3840 px on the long edge full-frame camera capture: floor-to-ceiling windows with a distant city skyline, herringbone oak floors, a low sectional, a marble fireplace, warm practical table lamps glowing against the cooler blue-hour ambient outside, straight verticals, real reflections and minor lens vignette, slightly flat and under-graded straight-off-the-camera contrast, an 18% neutral grey card laid flat on the floor in the near-left corner of the frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 16-35mm wide angle, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: THE FLAGSHIP / page-one thumbnail and the frame that ESTABLISHES the Sterling Row house look. Mixed cool blue-hour ambient + warm lamp practicals so the neutralize step has a genuine mixed cast to resolve to the in-frame card, and the flat under-graded capture gives the authored moody-luxury grade (deep blacks held off zero, controlled window highlights, restrained warm feel) real headroom. The distant skyline through the glass is a real, nameable object so image_select_by_prompt can isolate it for the signature masked amber-glow lift. Real-camera scale (~3840 px) so every downstream crop into the 1280x720 thumbnail frame is downscale-only. Grey card sits in the near-left corner so it is neutralized first, then cropped out for the 16:9 thumbnail crop while the retained pre-crop master keeps the card for grading.

inputs.name: hero_02_dusk_loft.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a loft living room at dusk, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, floor-to-ceiling windows showing a blue-hour city outside BUT the interior is dominated by strong warm tungsten table and floor lamps (~3000K, heavy amber cast on the walls and sofa), wide angle, real texture, slightly under-graded, frame tilted about 3 degrees, an 18% neutral grey card resting on the coffee table at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: LOOK-ALIKE A of a matched pair with hero_03: both read as 'blue-hour loft with city view' at a glance, but THIS one is interior-tungsten-dominant (heavy warm cast) so its grey card comes in warm and the correct move is to COOL white balance to neutral. Applying the same correction to both look-alikes is the trap — hero_03 needs the opposite. Tilted ~3deg so it needs straightening before the neutralize/crop. Camera scale.

inputs.name: hero_03_dusk_penthouse.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a penthouse living room at dusk, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, floor-to-ceiling windows with a blue-hour city view, near-identical framing and palette to a warm dusk loft BUT lit almost entirely by cool white LED downlights (~5200K, distinct cool cast on the walls and stone), wide angle, real texture, slightly under-graded, level horizon, an 18% neutral grey card on the console at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: LOOK-ALIKE B, the pair partner of hero_02. Superficially the same scene, but cool-LED-dominant, so its grey card comes in cool/blue and the correct move is to WARM white balance to neutral — the OPPOSITE direction from hero_02. Getting the pair wrong (one blanket correction, or swapping the two) is invisible until the two thumbnails sit side by side and clash. Level, so no straighten. Camera scale.

inputs.name: hero_04_golden_terrace.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate exterior hero photograph of a penthouse terrace at golden hour, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, warm low sun raking across the deck and skyline, genuine amber sunset glow that is the selling feature of the shot, real long shadows and warm highlights, shot under that warm light so the scene is authentically golden while a neutral 18% grey card laid on the terrace table still reads neutral under the open sky, wide angle, slightly under-graded, level, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The terrace warmth is the real product — a golden-hour amber glow the listing is selling — and because the card was lit by open sky it already reads essentially neutral. The correct move is NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/tone to the house target). A naive agent that batch-applies a 'warm the cool casts' or 'cool the warm casts' rule, or that 'cools an imagined amber cast', neutralizes the card off-neutral and strips the golden character the client is selling. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Level; camera scale.

inputs.name: hero_05_noon_kitchen.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a chef's kitchen at midday, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, harsh direct noon sun pouring through a skylight, cool bright daylight cast (~6000K), some blown highlights on the marble counters and hardware, wide angle, real texture, frame tilted about 4 degrees, an 18% neutral grey card on the island at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: Cool bright daylight: grey card reads cool and the frame is a touch hot, so the correct move WARMS white balance toward neutral AND pulls exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown marble, then seats the house black point — different again from the warm frames. Tilted ~4deg so it needs straightening first. Camera scale.

inputs.name: hero_06_overcast_suite.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a primary bedroom suite under flat overcast window light, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, soft shadowless grey daylight, the whole frame slightly underexposed and low-contrast, near-neutral but dull cast, wide angle, real fabric and wood texture, level, an 18% neutral grey card on the bench at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: The dominant problem here is TONAL, not white balance: flat and underexposed, so the main move is to LIFT exposure and add contrast/clarity to hit the house look, with only a small WB nudge to land the (near-neutral) card on the shared white point. Over-warming or over-cooling chasing a cast that is not there would push it off the set. Level; camera scale.

inputs.name: hero_07_tungsten_study.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a wood-panelled study/library at night, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, warm tungsten picture lights and a table lamp (~2900K, cozy amber cast), rich dark wood, real book and leather texture, slightly under-graded, level, an 18% neutral grey card on the desk at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: Genuinely warm tungsten room whose card reads clearly warm — correct move is to COOL white balance to neutral (same DIRECTION as hero_02 but a different magnitude and a different starting exposure, so its numbers must be reasoned separately, not copied). Distinguishing this 'warm cast to correct' from hero_04's 'warm scene to KEEP' is the core per-frame judgment. Level; camera scale.

inputs.name: hero_08_northlight_loft.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal raw unretouched real-estate interior hero photograph of a north-light artist's loft, ~3840 px long edge full-frame capture, cool even north daylight (~6200K, cool cast), bright and slightly overexposed with airy white walls, wide angle, real concrete and steel texture, frame tilted about 3 degrees, an 18% neutral grey card on the sill at the edge of frame as a white-balance reference, no text, 3:2 landscape
inputs.realism_notes: Coolest and brightest of the set: strong cool cast plus mild overexposure, so the correct move is the LARGEST warm WB shift of the batch AND an exposure pull-down, while protecting the airy white walls from turning grey — the strongest correction, opposite in both axes to the warm-and-dim study. Tilted ~3deg so it needs straightening first. Camera scale.

inputs.name: broker_portrait.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal studio headshot of a confident 45-year-old male luxury real-estate broker, charcoal tailored suit, no tie, arms loosely crossed, three-quarter turn to camera, clean seamless dark-gray studio backdrop, soft key with subtle rim light, real skin pores and a few flyaway hairs, slight five-o'clock shadow, candid editorial expression, 85mm f1.8 look, shallow depth of field, never CGI-glossy, sharp focus on the eyes, frame tilted about 3 degrees, full-frame portrait orientation ~3000 px long edge
inputs.realism_notes: Real studio capture with a clean but genuine seamless backdrop so image_remove_background has a believable subject edge to find; visible pores and flyaway hairs keep the isolation honest. Slightly tilted (~3deg) so it must be levelled before isolation so the figure sits true when placed in the thumbnail. The isolated transparent figure is a delivered layer AND the shared @broker merge image, the same figure on every episode's thumbnail.

inputs.name: sterling_row_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Minimal luxury real-estate wordmark, the text 'STERLING ROW' in an elegant high-contrast serif with refined letter-spacing and a thin underline rule, solid monochrome charcoal lettering on a plain flat WHITE background (not transparent), crisp clean edges, no gradients, no photographic texture, generous white margin around the mark, centered, high resolution
inputs.realism_notes: Flat solid-ink mark on a WHITE ground with a generous margin, so a naive raster-to-vector trace of the raw file would return a filled rectangle silhouette (the white ground traces as a shape) — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: knock the outer white ground to transparency, crop to the mark's tight bounds, THEN vectorize to a clean SVG. Crisp single-ink edges make the trace faithful. The elegant serif has enclosed counters (R, O, G, e, a) that the trace keeps filled from the crisped-white ground, so the mark is placed on the template's LIGHT masthead band — never knocked over the dark hero — where those counters read as light; the shared @wordmark merge image on every thumbnail.

inputs.name: walkthrough_take.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: One continuous ~9-minute 1920x1080 handheld-stabilized real-estate walkthrough take of the Tribeca flagship penthouse: opens on the broker on camera in the great room gesturing toward the view, a slow push through the floor-to-ceiling windows revealing the skyline, then the kitchen and primary suite, documentary cinematography, prestige tone, natural room audio
inputs.realism_notes: A SINGLE long continuous camera take (~9 minutes) at native 1920x1080, NOT a bundle of short clips — because video_create_quick_cut only SHORTENS one supplied longer take and cannot assemble multiple clips. The varied sequence (broker, skyline reveal, kitchen, suite) gives the quick-cut distinct compelling moments to choose the ~14s cold-open from. Native 1920x1080 so the 16:9 video-platform teaser is delivered at source resolution and the 1080x1080 square cross-post is a same-length center crop that never upscales.

inputs.name: endcard_backplate_take.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: One continuous ~3-minute 3840x2160 (4K) slow drifting aerial take of a city skyline at dusk for a luxury channel outro backplate: gentle drone drift over glowing towers, soft cinematic grain, muted prestige palette, the entire LOWER THIRD kept as calm empty sky and distant low buildings as deliberate negative space for a subscribe button, a suggested-video card and a CTA to be set later, restrained elegant motion, no text, no UI, no logos, no people
inputs.realism_notes: A SINGLE long continuous 4K take (~3 minutes), NOT pooled short clips — quick_cut shortens this one take to the ~12s end card. Declared at 3840x2160 so the reframe to the exact 1920x1080 delivery frame is a genuine DOWNSCALE (video_resize never upscales); a native-1080p source would make the 1920x1080 delivery a no-op or an upscale. Lower-third negative space is preserved so the subscribe/suggested-video/CTA zones sit correctly and identically across episodes.

inputs.name: sterling_row_thumbnail_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 1280x720 px (16:9) landscape video-platform thumbnail — ONE episode per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<episode_headline>>, <<listing_tagline>>, <<price_teaser>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a full-bleed hero frame bound to @hero (that episode's graded property still), a small figure frame bound to @broker (the isolated broker transparent PNG), and a frame bound to @wordmark (the vectorized wordmark) riding a solid LIGHT (near-white) masthead band drawn across the top of the layout, so the mark sits on light and never over the dark hero photo. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the graded hero, the broker figure and the wordmark reach the page ONLY as merge binds through these three image frames. Built by hand in InDesign so the text fields and all three image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one episode's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up contact sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record 1280x720 thumbnail template is the correct connector-doable shape and every episode's HEADLINE TYPE is actually SET by the merge (fixing the killed original, which handed the headline to a human). THREE image columns (@hero varies per row; @broker and @wordmark are the same file in every row) mean the chain-produced graded hero, isolated broker and vectorized wordmark all reach the thumbnail as merge binds, never free-form placement. The @wordmark frame rides a solid light masthead band the template draws across the top, distinct from the dark full-bleed hero, so the vectorized mark's enclosed serif counters (which the raster-to-vector trace keeps filled with the crisped-white ground) read correctly on light and never print as blobs on the dark photo — a dark-ground knockout of an enclosed-counter mark is not connector-doable. Supplied as an input, not a chain output.

inputs.name: sterling_row_episode_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns episode_headline,listing_tagline,price_teaser,@hero,@broker,@wordmark holding 8 episode rows, one per featured listing, the flagship Tribeca penthouse FIRST. Each row carries a short punchy click-worthy episode headline (e.g. 'Inside a $24M Tribeca Sky Penthouse'), a one-line listing tagline, and a price teaser string. The @hero column names that episode's graded hero file (e.g. @hero_01_penthouse_greatroom_graded.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded still into that row's thumbnail hero frame. The @broker column holds the SAME isolated broker file (@broker_isolated.png) in EVERY row, and the @wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file (@sterling_row_wordmark.svg) in every row, so the merge drops the shared figure and mark onto every episode's thumbnail as merge binds. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<episode_headline>>,<<listing_tagline>>,<<price_teaser>> and the three @image-path columns @hero,@broker,@wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: Row order sets page order, so the flagship penthouse row first makes the flagship thumbnail page 1 (the 'hero' is simply the first page of the merged set — no per-record named export). Headers match the authored .indd fields and all THREE @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds the headline/tagline/price plus the correct graded hero and the shared broker+wordmark per episode. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished thumbnails.

outputs.name: sterling_row_thumbnail_set.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight finished 1280x720 (16:9) video-platform thumbnails — ONE single-record page per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8), flagship Tribeca penthouse first — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each thumbnail has its <<episode_headline>>/<<listing_tagline>>/<<price_teaser>> actually SET from the roster, that episode's grey-card-neutralized graded property hero dropped full-bleed into the @hero frame, the isolated broker figure dropped into the @broker frame, and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the @wordmark frame on a light masthead band across the top (a distinct light strip, not the dark hero) — all by merge bind, never free-form placement. sRGB, screen-res. The flagship penthouse thumbnail (page 1) carries the authored Sterling Row look; the other seven are matched to it.

outputs.name: graded_property_heroes_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized property hero stills matched to one prestige white point and the flagship's authored moody-luxury look, delivered as the 16:9 thumbnail crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared prestige white point while the flagship's authored look (deep blacks held off pure zero, controlled window highlights, restrained warm feel, lifted-but-not-garish skyline) holds across all eight, and true-to-listing (no room's genuine character forced off); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 16:9 thumbnail crop (the *_graded output that binds into that episode's thumbnail) — it is framed on the room with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the thumbnail crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance/exposure/tone move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: broker_isolated.png
outputs.spec: Transparent-background PNG of the broker, auto-straightened then isolated from the studio backdrop (remove_background to transparency, subject auto-detected — no reconstruction, no bg-replace-by-prompt), a delivered layer and the shared @broker merge image placed on every episode's thumbnail.

outputs.name: sterling_row_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the STERLING ROW wordmark, traced only after the flat outer white ground is knocked to transparency and the mark is cropped to its tight bounds — razor-sharp at masthead scale. The elegant serif's enclosed counters are kept filled from the crisped-white ground by the trace, so the mark rides a LIGHT masthead band on the thumbnail (never knocked over the dark hero), where those counters read as light; a dark-ground enclosed-counter knockout is not claimed. The shared @wordmark merge image on every thumbnail.

outputs.name: teaser_wide_1920x1080.mp4
outputs.spec: A ~14s cinematic cold-open teaser SHORTENED from the single ~9-minute 1920x1080 walkthrough take via an AI highlight cut (strong visual hook in the first 5s, hard-cut before the reveal), delivered at the take's native 1920x1080, prestige tone, no added transitions. Output duration < source; no assembly, no lengthening.

outputs.name: teaser_square_1080x1080.mp4
outputs.spec: The same teaser cut reframed to a 1080x1080 square for the 1:1 square cross-post, SAME length (a same-length center-crop reframe of the 1920x1080 teaser; the 1080 crop height holds, so no upscale).

outputs.name: endcard_1920x1080.mp4
outputs.spec: A ~12s branded end card SHORTENED from the single ~3-minute 4K skyline backplate take via an AI highlight cut, then reframed by DOWNSCALE to exactly 1920x1080 (from the 3840x2160 source, never upscaled), with the lower third kept clear for the subscribe prompt, suggested-video card and CTA, consistent across episodes.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hero_01_penthouse_greatroom.jpg, hero_02_dusk_loft.jpg, hero_03_dusk_penthouse.jpg, hero_04_golden_terrace.jpg, hero_05_noon_kitchen.jpg, hero_06_overcast_suite.jpg, hero_07_tungsten_study.jpg, hero_08_northlight_loft.jpg, broker_portrait.jpg, sterling_row_wordmark.png
connector_workflow.note: Bring the eight property hero stills, the broker portrait, and the flat wordmark into the working project in one load so the grade, isolation and vectorize can run against real asset references. Plumbing only — not the difficulty. (The two long video takes are handled by the async media tools; the .indd template and roster CSV are supplied inputs consumed at merge.)

Flagship: neutralize hero_01 to the 18% grey card it carries — reason this frame's own temperature and tint until the card reads neutral, then AUTHOR the Sterling Row house look from primitives on this reference frame: set blacks deep but held off pure zero, pull highlights to control the bright windows, hold a restrained warm prestige feel, add modest clarity and vibrance. This is a reasoned authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. The temperature/tint/exposure/black values chosen here DEFINE the shared target the other seven must hit; report them. Consumes the uploaded flagship still.

On the graded flagship frame, semantically select the city skyline seen through the floor-to-ceiling windows ('the distant city skyline visible through the windows'). A real, nameable object (not a hue or a geometric band), returning a maskURI to confine the signature amber-glow lift to the skyline only. Consumes step 2.

Masked signature move (consumes the flagship frame + skyline mask): within the skyline mask only, lift and moderately warm the amber/orange city-glow band with a small in-band hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance lift (well under ~90deg — an in-band adjacent shift, no near-complementary rotation), so the city glows richly without turning garish, while the interior wood and skin tones OUTSIDE the mask are untouched. image_adjust_hsl is the only masked recolor path; whole-image color_overlay or a flat fill_area would tint the whole room and are wrong here. Completes the authored flagship look. Consumes step 2 image + step 3 mask.

Crop the graded flagship frame to the 16:9 thumbnail hero crop, framing on the great room with the grey card cropped OUT — this card-removed crop is what binds into the flagship thumbnail via @hero. The pre-crop master (hero_01_neutralized) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop. Downscale-only from camera scale, onSubjectClipping='extract', never generative-expand. Consumes step 4.
This frame is tilted ~3deg, so level it before neutralizing and cropping. (Deciding which stills are tilted and skipping the level ones is part of the job.) Consumes the uploaded hero_02.

Neutralize hero_02 to the grey card it carries and MATCH the shared prestige white point and the flagship's house look — reason this frame's own white-balance and exposure to its card (do NOT reuse another frame's numbers) and seat the house black point and tonality. Report the moves applied. Consumes step 6.

Crop the neutralized frame to the 16:9 thumbnail crop, grey card cropped OUT; the retained hero_02_neutralized master keeps the card for grading. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'. Consumes step 7.

Neutralize hero_03 to its own grey card and match the shared target and house look — reason its white-balance and exposure independently (this look-alike of hero_02 is lit differently and must be judged on its own card, not corrected the same way). Report the moves applied. Consumes the uploaded hero_03 (level, no straighten).
Crop to the 16:9 thumbnail crop, grey card cropped OUT; retained master keeps the card. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'. Consumes step 9.

Judge hero_04 on its OWN grey card and match it to the house target: if its card already reads neutral, hold white balance and only match exposure/tone — do not push a correction the card does not call for, so the room's genuine character is preserved. Report the (held or minimal) WB move plus the tonal match. Consumes the uploaded hero_04 (level).
Crop to the 16:9 thumbnail crop, grey card cropped OUT; retained master keeps the card. Downscale-only, onSubjectClipping='extract'. Consumes step 11.
Tilted ~4deg — level it before neutralizing and cropping. Consumes the uploaded hero_05.

Neutralize hero_05 to its grey card and match the shared target and house look — reason its own white-balance and exposure, recover any blown highlights so nothing clips, and seat the house black point. Report the moves applied. Consumes step 13.
